why: Most commands work as written. `npm test` maps to `node --test`. Checks 1, 2 and 4 use valid `node --input-type=module -e` imports of './index.js', which resolve from the repo root. Check 3 breaks because of shell escaping. Inside bash double quotes, `'^#+\\s+'` and `'\\b'` reach JavaScript as `'^#+\s+'` and `'\b'`. In a JS string literal, `\s` becomes a plain `s` and `\b` becomes a backspace character. The regex is therefore `/^#+s+name\x08/m`, which can never match a README heading like `## padLeft(...)`. The command still runs, but it reports every export as missing, even for a correct PR. It does not work as written. The builder brief's commands (`npm test`) are fine.
